.surfaces.

langfuse.label: Langfuse (self-hosted or cloud)
langfuse.host_note: Self-hosted Langfuse serves on http://localhost:3000 by default (plain http unless you put TLS in front of it); Langfuse Cloud: https://cloud.langfuse.com (EU), https://us.cloud.langfuse.com (US), https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com (JP), https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com (HIPAA).

config_keys.LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY: required - the plugin stores it in the OS keychain, not in a file
config_keys.LANGFUSE_BASE_URL: optional, default https://cloud.langfuse.com (EU) - set it for self-hosted. The variable is LANGFUSE_BASE_URL, not LANGFUSE_HOST

claude.requires: uv on PATH, or python3 >= 3.10 with langfuse>=4.7,<5
claude.note: `claude plugin install ... --config LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=...` also works but puts the secret in shell history and the process list - prefer /plugin configure (interactive) and pass only the non-secret LANGFUSE_BASE_URL via --config.

copilot.note: There is NO Langfuse plugin for Copilot. Copilot CLI/VS Code export OpenTelemetry natively; Langfuse is an OTLP backend (HTTP/JSON or protobuf; gRPC is not supported).

optional.OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSA: true - OPT-IN, off by default: stores prompts, responses and tool arguments in Langfuse. VS Code-launched CLI sessions forward the enable flag and endpoint but not this one.

copilot.debug: COPILOT_OTEL_EXPORTER_TYPE=file writes spans locally to confirm they are generated before pointing at Langfuse

dash0.host_note: Endpoint/dataset per the plugin's own README.
dash0.note: Name and required variables are not verified by this registry - read the plugin's README, add the variables to .env.harness by name, and if `claude plugin install` fails mark pending-manual.

structural.note: A7 bake-off pending — the first three are MCP servers configured via .mcp.json, not marketplace plugins. Two unrelated projects share the 'CodeGraph' name: codegraph-ai/CodeGraph (tree-sitter semantic graph, 42+ MCP tools, RocksDB persistent memory layer, VS Code extension) vs colbymchenry/codegraph (lightweight pre-indexed graph, CLI-installed, SQLite, native OS file-watcher auto-sync, no external services) — confirm which repo the user means before installing. colbymchenry/codegraph installs via: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colbymchenry/codegraph/main/install.sh | sh (macOS/Linux) or npm i -g @colbymchenry/codegraph, then `codegraph install` + `codegraph init [path]`. codebase-memory-mcp has its own installer: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/main/install.sh | bash. Graphify is CLI + skill based, not MCP-first: PyPI package is `graphifyy` (double-y; the CLI command stays `graphify`) — install via `uv tool install graphifyy` (or `pipx install graphifyy`), then `graphify install --project` to register a project-scoped `/graphify` skill (writes `.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`, committable), or `graphify claude install --project` to also wire the PreToolUse hook that nudges (or, with `--strict`, blocks-once-per-session) raw file reads toward `graphify query` instead — a natural pairing with se-harness's own hook-enforced gates. Local tree-sitter AST parsing for code, no vector store; docs/PDF/image/video ingestion calls the assistant's model API. An `.mcp.json` route exists too if MCP access is preferred over the skill: `uv tool install "graphifyy[mcp]"` then `python -m graphify.serve graphify-out/graph.json`. If Graphify is chosen, se-harness's own /harness-mem-graphify command (not this registry entry's install line) is what /harness-bootstrap hands off to for the actual install-plus-first-build — it also handles merging multiple repos' graphs into one workspace-level graph, which a bare Graphify install doesn't do on its own.
